title: Nanahuatl: The Sun's Birth
subtitle: A creation episode in Spence's Mexican synthesis

learningObjectives.text: How does Nanahuatl become the sun?
Why does the moon have a rabbit?

sun.author: Lewis Spence
sun.locator: Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY; Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY, normalized characters 67893-68294
sun.excerpt: The myth of Nanahuatl tells how before the sun was created humanity dwelt in sable and horrid gloom. Only a human sacrifice could hasten the appearance of the luminary. Metztli (The Moon) led forth Nanahuatl as a sacrifice, and he was cast upon a funeral pyre, in the flames of which he was consumed. Metztli also cast herself upon the mass of flame, and with her death the sun rose above the horizon.
sun.note: Verbatim prose from Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century synthesis, not a direct translation of the Indigenous source material he discusses. Preserve its dated, colonial framing.

narrativeBlocks.title: A world in darkness
narrativeBlocks.body: Before the sun, humanity lives in darkness. The gods gather at Teotihuacan to choose who will be sacrificed to become the new sun.

narrativeBlocks.title: The boast and the humility
narrativeBlocks.body: The proud, rich god Tecciztecatl volunteers loudly for the honour; the humble, pockmarked Nanahuatl — covered in sores — is chosen but stays silent.

narrativeBlocks.title: The leap into the fire
narrativeBlocks.body: At the great pyre, Tecciztecatl falters at the flames again and again; Nanahuatl leaps in at once — and rises as the sun. Ashamed, Tecciztecatl follows and becomes the moon.

narrativeBlocks.title: The dimming of the second light
narrativeBlocks.body: The second sun blazes too brightly to be night — so the gods hurl a rabbit at it to dim it. That is why the moon carries a rabbit on its face.

narrativeBlocks.title: The fifth sun needs feeding
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the fifth sun: four previous worlds ended in destruction. The Mexica read this as a debt — the sun stays in motion only through sacrifice.

quiz.prompt: How does Nanahuatl become the sun?

choices.text: He is thrown in by the other gods
He defeats the moon-god in combat
He leaps into the pyre without hesitating, while the proud Tecciztecatl falters at the flames

quiz.explanation: The humble god leaps first — and becomes the greater light.

quiz.prompt: Why does the moon have a rabbit on it?

choices.text: The gods hurled a rabbit at the second sun to dim it — its mark stays on the moon
The rabbit is the moon's true form

quiz.explanation: The dimmed second sun keeps the rabbit's print.
